content:
The [API Tester](/api-tester) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Send a request to any public API and inspect the status and response. Enter your request URL and method and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Send a request to any public API and inspect the answer: pick a method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE), add headers and a body if you need them, and see the status code, response time, headers and body. It is the quick way to check whether an API is up, whether your request is shaped correctly, and what an endpoint actually returns — without installing a desktop client. Requests go through this site's server with strict safety limits (public addresses only, 10-second timeout, 2 MB cap, request body capped at 100 KB), and nothing is stored.

## How to use the API Tester

Start by typing or pasting your request URL, then choosing your method from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter the request URL and pick a method.
2. Add headers (one per line, Name: value) and a body for POST, PUT or PATCH.
3. Send the request and read the status, time, headers and body.

## How it works

The [API Tester](/api-tester) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A GET to https://api.github.com/zen returns 200 with a one-line piece of wisdom as the body — a handy endpoint for testing that a request works. Try the same figures in the [API Tester](/api-tester) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [API Tester](/api-tester) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What the tester sends

Exactly the request you describe — method, URL, headers and body — from this site's server, not from your browser (a browser cannot call most APIs directly because of CORS). No cookies or credentials are sent, and the URL must be a public http or https address: private and local addresses are blocked.

## Reading the result

A 2xx status means the request worked; 4xx means the request was wrong (400 bad request, 401 unauthorised, 404 not found); 5xx means the server had a problem. The response time is the round trip from this site's server, and the body is shown as text (up to 100 KB) — JSON responses are shown as they are, ready to copy.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Test a GET first — if that fails, the URL or the service is the problem, not your body.
- A 401 usually means a missing or wrong Authorization header.
- Do not send real passwords or API keys through any online tester.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is an API tester?

A tool that sends an HTTP request to an API and shows the response: status code, headers and body. It is how developers check that an endpoint works and what it returns. Try it with your own numbers in the [API Tester](/api-tester) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why does the request go through a server?

Browsers block most cross-site requests (CORS), so the request is sent from this site's server instead. No cookies or credentials are attached, and private addresses are blocked. Try it with your own numbers in the [API Tester](/api-tester) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is it safe to send an API key here?

No — never paste a real secret into any online tester. Use a test key, or test against an endpoint that does not need one. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### What do I need to use the API Tester?

Just Request URL and Method. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
